articles.title: AI Power Semis — Wolfspeed vs onsemi vs Infineon
articles.summary: Three ways to express the AI power theme, but with very different quality, risk, and valuation profiles.

content.text: If the question is how to express the AI power theme through semiconductors, these three names are not interchangeable.

items: Infineon is the best quality-adjusted expression.
onsemi is the best U.S.-listed real-business expression.
Wolfspeed is the highest-torque and highest-risk expression.

content.text: What matters

The key split is not just who has silicon carbide. It is who has real AI-power exposure, who can actually monetize it, and who still needs a balance-sheet miracle before the thesis deserves institutional size.
Portfolio view

items: Infineon fits best as a durable core expression.
onsemi is the cleaner U.S. listed compromise between exposure and business quality.
Wolfspeed is a speculative turnaround trade, not a clean compounder.

content.text: Cheap distressed optionality is not the same thing as cheap quality.

articles.title: China AI Infrastructure — The Hidden Power Play
articles.summary: The better AI expression may sit in power, grid, and equipment layers rather than platform headlines.

content.text: China's AI buildout is not only a software or GPU story. It is also a power-demand story, and the market still underprices the equipment and generation layers that make that buildout physically possible.
The chain
LLM deployment growth drives data-center load, which drives electricity demand, which then pushes value toward generation assets, power equipment, and grid-enabling suppliers.
What the investor should care about

items: Visible backlog beats vague AI narrative.
Dispatchable power and equipment order flow matter more than headline model launches.
The best setups are where AI demand upgrades an already investable business, not where AI is the only story holding up the multiple.

content.text: Practical read
This lens naturally pushes attention toward names tied to energized power, nuclear buildout, backup generation, and electrical equipment — not just cloud or application winners.

articles.title: Agentic Inference Memory / I-O Pressure Indicator
articles.summary: A technical indicator note tracking whether agentic and long-context systems are turning memory, cache, and I/O into first-class bottlenecks.

content.text: This is not an investing note first. It is a stack-reality note. The question is whether production AI is evolving from a pure compute problem into a memory-, cache-, and I/O-constrained systems problem.
Chain tested

Agentic workflows and long-context inference rise, persistent state and retrieval pressure rise, then the bottleneck shifts toward memory hierarchy and data movement rather than raw model compute alone.
Why this belongs in AI research

items: It asks what the system is doing, not what stock rerates.
It tracks technical evidence like KV-cache pressure, tiered memory, and DPU-attached context storage.
It helps distinguish real production pain from conference-slide storytelling.

content.text: When vendors stop describing architecture and start shipping products to solve a named bottleneck, the bottleneck is getting real.

articles.title: AI Power Delivery Bottleneck
articles.summary: A systems note on why energized megawatts, electrical balance-of-plant, and commissioning can gate AI deployment before more GPUs do.

content.text: The market loves the phrase 'AI data centers' but often skips the ugly physical question: can the site actually be energized on time?
Bottleneck layer
Why this is AI research rather than finance first
The core question is deployment reality: where does the physical stack jam when rack density and site load rise? The investment angle comes later. The note starts with system constraints.
Research use
This note should inform later finance work, but it should not be reduced to a stock screen. First map the bottleneck. Then decide who monetizes it.
